A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DASH, with matching authors, methods and experiments. The complete documents, including Appendices A–C, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DASH evaluations on AVUT, VideoMME and WorldSense, including accuracy, inference efficiency, component ablations and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original DASH benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, ablations and qualitative analyses. Retained results still constitute original empirical results.

M1.justification: Equations (1)–(12) and the computational steps in Algorithm 1 retain the same boundary detection, projection, scoring and compression procedures. Revised descriptions of soft temporal priors, boundary-neighborhood retention and attention scores do not establish a new computation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same AVUT subtasks, VideoMME without subtitles and eight WorldSense domains. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain Full Tokens, Random, FastV, DyCoke and OmniZip. The component ablations and boundary-detector comparisons also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: The model sizes, retention settings, frame limits, metrics and benchmark procedures remain unchanged. v2 newly specifies deterministic decoding and rule-based multiple-choice parsing, but does not report changing previously stated evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Tables 4–5 retain the component and boundary-detector ablations, and Figure 4 retains the weight-sensitivity analysis. Appendix A uses the same qualitative examples; its additional Figure 5 repeats the existing token-selection visualization rather than adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The segment-length standard deviations in the qualitative visualization are unchanged and do not represent new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The benchmark scores, ablation values, plotted trends and Table 3 speedups are unchanged. Section 4.3 removes the concrete runtime example stating that prefill for a 60-second video falls from 10 seconds to under 3 seconds; no replacement measurement is supplied.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(12) are unchanged, and neither version includes formal theorems or proofs. The revised explanation of audio–visual correspondence changes interpretation rather than a formal mathematical assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement and conclusion narrow the alignment claim: projected audio boundaries provide soft temporal priors rather than establishing explicit cross-modal semantic alignment. The central training-free compression contribution and accuracy-efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: Sections 3.3–3.5 and Appendix A explicitly reject requiring exact audio–visual boundary coincidence and describe boundary retention as a conservative safeguard. Section 4.2 narrows the inference from architecture-general improvements to robustness across model scales within the same OmniLLM family.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents deterministic decoding and rule-based multiple-choice parsing in Section 4.1. Section 3.3 also clarifies that segments use original encoder embeddings independently, without feeding earlier compressed outputs into later boundaries or features. Hardware, hyperparameters and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 revises H-Net from training-free boundary detection to learned end-to-end routing, MEGABYTE from variable-length to fixed-size patches, and clarifies MMHNet's role. It also removes the universal novelty assertion that explicit audio–visual alignment is absent from all prior work.

P1.justification: Targeted paragraph rewrites and terminology changes consistently introduce the audio-guided temporal-prior framing. v2 adds acknowledgments, updates affiliation wording and expands bibliographic details, while retaining the main section sequence and Appendices A–C.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn and its caption corrected to describe the depicted DASH pipeline rather than a baseline-versus-DASH comparison. v2 duplicates Figure 2 as appendix Figure 5, renumbers the existing boundary visualization as Figure 6, and adjusts figure/table placement and page margins.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision by replacing guaranteed semantic alignment with a temporal-prior interpretation and limiting generalization claims to the evaluated model family. It also fixes Figure 1's mismatched caption and adds useful evaluation details. These are meaningful reporting improvements, while the unchanged algorithms and empirical evidence limit their overall magnitude.
